Status: **frozen prospective methodological amendment; not executed**

## Explicit protocol-phase split

Positions 1–21 are immutable historical production under
`candidate-screening-v0.2.0` and its original reviewer-authority regime.
Position 21 terminally published as `OUT_OF_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED`. This amendment
does not relabel, reinterpret, or change any historical decision or artifact.

Before Position 22 was opened, reviewer authority was prospectively changed
for operational reasons. Position 22 onward uses an authoritative non-human
`AI_FIRST_REVIEW` for every `STRUCTURED_REVIEW_REQUIRED` case. When the
unchanged frozen Reviewer B trigger requires a second review, another fresh,
independently blinded non-human `AI_SECOND_REVIEW` is authoritative.

This authority change is not claimed to be scientifically neutral. It creates
a protocol-phase difference between historical Positions 1–21 and amended
Positions 22 onward and is a methodological limitation when interpreting or
comparing outcomes across the phases. Candidate order and the evidence made
available to each logical review role do not change.

## Unchanged scientific authority

The amendment changes only ordinary semantic reviewer authority and the
minimal assignment/decision provenance needed to represent it honestly. It
does not amend the frozen candidate universe, sealed queue or order,
administrative exclusions, repository-anchor limits, global anchor accounting,
G0/G1 automatic authority, G2–G8 extraction semantics, TPTM implementation,
hybrid routing, Q1–Q10, `YES`/`NO`/`UNKNOWN` semantics, affirmative-evidence
requirements, trust or witness ontology, source condition, Reviewer B trigger,
Reviewer B blinding, disagreement handling, family feasibility/construction,
exact focal-hypothesis requirement, executable validation, repository
independence, category limits, stopping rule, or 1,000-anchor ceiling.

In particular, insufficient evidence remains `UNKNOWN`; absence of evidence is
not evidence for `NO`. A source already violating the focal proposition does
not qualify. `REVIEW_UNRESOLVED` may use only the frozen constrained
family-feasibility route, and no controller may synthesize a unique focal
hypothesis.

Final admission still requires every executable equivalent of:

```text
p*(S)=TRUE
p*(C)=TRUE
p*(I)=FALSE
required functional oracle(s)=PASS
reuse witness=TRIGGERED
safe witness=BLOCKED
exactly_one_focal_trust_change=TRUE
trust_category=KNOWN
repository_independence=PASS
```

AI judgment cannot override executable validation.

## Fresh one-shot roles and provenance

Every logical role uses a new `codex exec` operating-system process. Neither
`codex resume` nor `codex fork` is permitted. At minimum, a structured-review
position uses separate Position controller, `AI_FIRST_REVIEW`, continuation,
`AI_SECOND_REVIEW` when triggered, and combination/continuation processes.
The next position, after terminal publication only, starts another process.

AI semantic output is mechanically validated against the unchanged frozen
Q1–Q10 types and outcome derivation. The canonical amended decision envelope
records non-human reviewer type and role, assignment and packet hashes, prompt
hash, decision hash, timestamps, installed Codex CLI version, configured or
observed model identifier when available, runner invocation identity, and the
fresh Codex thread identity when exposed by the CLI. Missing optional CLI
metadata is recorded as unavailable; it is never fabricated.
The frozen runner selector is `gpt-5.6-sol` with no named CLI profile; every
role command passes that model selector explicitly.

The amended envelope is authoritative prospectively. Its
`semantic_projection_sha256` binds the unchanged finite semantic fields using
the existing canonical TPTM representation; this internal compatibility
projection does not convert the AI role into a human role.

## Reviewer B blinding

Reviewer B runs in a separate bubblewrap filesystem capsule. The capsule
contains only the latest append-only, repository-authorized blinded assignment,
its hash-verified permitted evidence, and frozen interface files. The
production worktree, other position records, AI Reviewer A material, combined
state, outcomes, admission state, scores/gold, future queue material, Track B,
and Codex conversation history are not mounted. Assignment correction, when
needed, is append-only and numbered; an earlier assignment is never edited.

Any disagreement on a required answer or exact focal hypothesis yields
`REVIEW_UNRESOLVED`. There is no vote, reviewer priority, confidence weighting,
third reviewer, controller tie-break, or informal override.

## External unattended runner

The hash-bound runner is operational infrastructure outside this worktree at:

```text
/home/anjum/track-a-production-runner/
```

It holds one exclusive Track A `flock`, verifies the expected branch/HEAD and
tracked/index baseline, validates protocol/amendment/queue/ledger hashes,
replays every published record, launches role-specific one-shot processes,
and reads only durable orchestration metadata. It never performs semantic
candidate review. Logs and mutable expected-HEAD state remain outside Git.

The runner stops successfully on the unchanged global stopping rule or its
operational `--max-positions` bound. It fails closed on scientific or unresolved
engineering blockers, `ANALYSIS_ERROR`, integrity/replay/HEAD/blinding/decision
failures, ambiguous partial publication, future-position isolation violations,
missing frozen interfaces, or any state it cannot affirmatively prove safe.
Only a failed role proven to have made no durable change may be retried, and
the retry is another new process.

At adoption the ledger has exactly 21 published/processed positions, two

`global_action=CONTINUE`. Position 22 authorization, runtime directory, and

production, or opening Position 22.

"""Template-fill helper: emit a valid PR body skeleton from PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.

Reads ``.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md``, fills in the issue number, a
placeholder verification entry that satisfies the post-2026-05-26
command/result pair shape gate, and the agent attribution footer. The output
passes ``scripts/body_policy.py verify --kind pull_request --shape-cutoff
2026-05-26T00:00:00Z --body-file <path>`` so agents can start from a
policy-conformant skeleton instead of hand-rolling the shape.

Usage::

    python3 scripts/pr_body_builder.py build --issue 938
    python3 scripts/pr_body_builder.py build --issue 938 \\
        --agent "Claude Code" --session-url "https://claude.ai/code/session_XYZ"
    python3 scripts/pr_body_builder.py build --issue 938 \\
        --agent Codex --model gpt-4o

Refs #938.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from body_policy import build_codex_attribution_footer

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
_TEMPLATE_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md"

_HTML_COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r"<!--.*?-->", re.DOTALL)
_CLOSES_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"^Closes #\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
_EMPTY_VERIFICATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(-[ \t]+command:[ \t]*``[ \t]*\n[ \t]{2}result:[ \t]*``[ \t]*)$",
    re.MULTILINE,
)
_FOOTER_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(
    r"_Generated by \[Agent Name\]\(agent-session-url\)_"
)

_DEFAULT_AGENT = "Claude Code"
_DEFAULT_SESSION_URL = "https://claude.ai/code"
_VERIFICATION_PLACEHOLDER = (
    "- command: `<verification command>`\n  result: `<verification result>`"
)


def _build_footer(agent: str, session_url: str, model: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the attribution footer line for the given agent."""
    if agent.strip().lower() == "codex":
        if not model:
            raise ValueError(
                "Codex attribution requires --model; "
                "e.g. --model gpt-4o"
            )
        return build_codex_attribution_footer(model)
    return f"_Generated by [{agent}]({session_url})_"


def build(
    issue: int,
    *,
    agent: str = _DEFAULT_AGENT,
    session_url: str = _DEFAULT_SESSION_URL,
    model: str | None = None,
    template_path: Path = _TEMPLATE_PATH,
) -> str:
    """Return a PR body skeleton with *issue*, agent footer, and verification placeholder filled in.

    The returned string passes ``body_policy.verify`` with the post-2026-05-26
    shape gate enabled once the placeholder sections (Summary, Facts,
    Assumptions, Risk, Rollback, Verification command/result) are replaced with
    real content.
    """
    raw = template_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # Strip HTML comments -- they are for human template readers, not for
    # the body policy parser, and keeping them clutters the generated body.
    body = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.sub("", raw)

    # Collapse sequences of more than two blank lines that HTML comment
    # removal often leaves behind.
    body = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", body)

    # Fill in the issue number.
    body = _CLOSES_PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(f"Closes #{issue}", body)

    # Replace the template's empty command/result placeholders with
    # non-empty ones that satisfy the shape gate regex.
    body = _EMPTY_VERIFICATION_RE.sub(_VERIFICATION_PLACEHOLDER, body)

    # Replace the attribution footer placeholder.
    footer = _build_footer(agent, session_url, model)
    body = _FOOTER_PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(footer, body)

    # Ensure the body ends with a single newline.
    return body.rstrip("\n") + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_build = sub.add_parser(
        "build",
        help=(
            "Emit a valid PR body skeleton for the given issue. "
            "Fill in the placeholder sections before creating the PR."
        ),
    )
    p_build.add_argument(
        "--issue",
        type=int,
        required=True,
        help="Issue number to reference (Closes #<number>).",
    )
    p_build.add_argument(
        "--agent",
        default=_DEFAULT_AGENT,
        help=(
            f"Agent name for the attribution footer (default: {_DEFAULT_AGENT!r}). "
            "Use 'Codex' together with --model for the Codex-specific footer."
        ),
    )
    p_build.add_argument(
        "--session-url",
        default=_DEFAULT_SESSION_URL,
        help=(
            f"Session URL for the attribution footer "
            f"(default: {_DEFAULT_SESSION_URL!r}). "
            "Not used when --agent Codex is given."
        ),
    )
    p_build.add_argument(
        "--model",
        default=None,
        help="Codex model identifier (required when --agent Codex).",
    )
    p_build.add_argument(
        "--template",
        default=str(_TEMPLATE_PATH),
        help="Path to the PR body template (default: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        body = build(
            args.issue,
            agent=args.agent,
            session_url=args.session_url,
            model=args.model,
            template_path=Path(args.template),
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    sys.stdout.write(body)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    1  One or more checks fail (errors printed to stdout as ``::error::`` lines).

and :mod:`_ref_classifier` so this tool and the server-side CI gate cannot
drift. Refs #938.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from _ref_classifier import classify_refs, strip_html_comments
from body_policy import (
    extract_headings,
    missing_sections,
    required_sections,
    verify_pr_agent_attribution_footer,
    verify_pr_checklist_subsections,
    verify_pr_verification_pairs,
)
from scan_non_ascii import detect_non_ascii, has_ack_marker


def evaluate(body: str, *, issue: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Return ``::error::`` strings for every policy violation; empty list means OK.

    Checks are ordered from cheapest to most specific so the list is
    readable top-to-bottom (structure first, content second).
    """
    errors: list[str] = []

    # 1. Required H2/H3 sections.
    required = required_sections("pull_request", body=body)
    headings = extract_headings(body)
    for name in missing_sections(required, headings):
        errors.append(
            f"::error::PR body is missing required section: ## {name} "
            f"(body_policy baseline gate)."
        )

    # 2. Verification command/result pairs (post-2026-05-26 shape gate).
    errors.extend(verify_pr_verification_pairs(body))

    # 3. Checklist H3 subsections (post-2026-05-26 shape gate).
    errors.extend(verify_pr_checklist_subsections(body))

    # 4. Agent attribution footer (post-2026-05-26 shape gate).
    errors.extend(verify_pr_agent_attribution_footer(body))

    # 5. ASCII-only content.  Honor the operator ack marker so bodies
    #    with <!-- non-ascii-ack --> are not false-positively flagged.
    if not has_ack_marker(body) and detect_non_ascii(body):
        errors.append(
            "::error::PR body contains non-ASCII characters. "
            "GitHub posts must be ASCII-only (preflight_non_ascii.py). "
            "Either translate to English or append <!-- non-ascii-ack --> to the body."
        )

    # 6. Issue reference (only when caller requests it).
    if issue is not None:
        cleaned = strip_html_comments(body)
        refs = classify_refs(cleaned)
        if not refs:
            errors.append(
                f"::error::PR body has no issue reference "
                f"(Closes/Fixes/Resolves/Refs #N). "
                f"Add a `Closes #{issue}` line in the Related Issue section."
            )
        elif not any(n == issue for _, n in refs):
            found = ", ".join(f"#{n}" for _, n in refs)
            errors.append(
                f"::error::PR body references {found} but not #{issue}. "
                f"Add a `Closes #{issue}` (or `Refs #{issue}`) line."
            )

    return errors


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_verify = sub.add_parser(
        "verify",
        help="Validate a PR body file against all local policy checks.",
    )
    p_verify.add_argument(
        "--body-file",
        required=True,
        help="Path to a file containing the candidate PR body.",
    )
    p_verify.add_argument(
        "--issue",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Expected issue number. When given, the body must contain a "
            "Closes/Fixes/Resolves/Refs reference to this number."
        ),
    )

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    body = Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    errors = evaluate(body, issue=args.issue)

    for msg in errors:
        print(msg)

    if not errors:
        print("OK: PR body passes all local preflight checks.")
        return 0
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
